observations: The generic postcard BufFlavor checks total remaining bytes before creating a slice from the first chunk pointer and advancing the buffer. A total-length check alone does not establish a contiguous first chunk for an arbitrary Buf; inspect the lock-bound bytes trait, pointer/lifetime requirements and actual buffer implementations before attributing a memory-safety defect to any supported application path.

Client and server messages use concrete Bytes in their registered deserialization signatures. The separately inspected tactical SceneBuilding decoder also accepts Bytes. Other helper callers, bytes implementation, compiler features and message transport paths need independent proof; these bounded signatures do not prove all application uses safe.

Message registration preserves separate serialization contexts, typed adapters and entity mapping choices; incoming malformed messages can be logged and ignored in the inspected receive paths. Server send serialization errors hit expects in the inspected sending path, whereas client send errors log and skip. Supported payload admission, event identity, ordering, queue behavior and actual sender/receiver error propagation remain open.

Each body was personally read including native source tests/examples; none ran. Exact registered source bytes match members of the current lock-checksum archive. No product build, test, simulation or runtime probe ran.
remaining: Trace bytes Buf and pointer guarantees, actual application/helper callers and postcard borrow behavior; inspect registry/queue and transport identity, enabled features, all aliases and all independent lenses.
